question.problem:
Given the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ shown below, draw the linear combination $2\mathbf{a}+3\mathbf{b}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251898/assets/325e4a450d89ee1f5db4afd237dbc7d58efafec72d080386788f0491cc35950b.png)
question.worked_solution:
- The vector $2\mathbf{a}$ has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$ but twice the magnitude.

- Likewise, the vector $3\mathbf{b}$ has the same direction as $\mathbf{b}$ but three times the magnitude.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251898/assets/066784522a39671fe57b157c6c692f5c56295126b8ec6f150d917e783ab63400.png)

Now, we can draw $3\mathbf{b}$ starting from the head of $2\mathbf{a}.$ The resultant 

$$
2\mathbf{a}+3\mathbf{b}
$$

goes from the tail of $2\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $3\mathbf{b}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251898/assets/d1dd084ad4f8f717afac515471bcba679fbe545f266435a57fb1c94d0d5c9cca.png)
